Simulation Verification Comparing Pseudo-IGM and Non-Linear WLS Optimization

Source: R/simulations.R
runWLSEOpt.Rd

Executes a Monte Carlo simulation benchmarking the closed-form priority weight vectors derived by Pseudo-IGM (pseudoIGM) against the numerical global optimization solver (WLSopt) via nloptr, verifying that closed-form IGM formulas consistently achieve the exact global minimum Weighted Least Squares Error (WLSE) without relying on iterative numerical solvers (Section 4.2; Yuen, 2024).

Usage

runWLSEOpt(
  size = 10,
  seedNo = 100,
  sigDigits = 4,
  errorFile = "wlseOptData.txt"
)

Arguments

size

Integer. Total number of random PRM simulation instances to evaluate (default: 10).

seedNo

Integer. Seed number for pseudo-random number generator initialization to ensure reproducibility (default: 100).

sigDigits

Integer. Number of significant decimal places used for rounding priority weight vectors during equality verification (default: 4).

errorFile

Character string. Output text file path for logging simulation results and discrepancy metrics (default: "wlseOptData.txt").

Value

Logical. Returns FALSE if all simulation iterations pass without discrepancy, or TRUE if a discrepancy is detected.

References

Yuen, K. K. F. (2024). Inverse Gram Matrix Methods for Prioritization in Analytic Hierarchy Process: Explainability of Weighted Least Squares Optimization Method. arXiv preprint arXiv:2401.01190. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2401.01190

Author

Kevin Kam Fung Yuen

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  # Run simulation comparing Pseudo-IGM against numerical solver for 5 random PRMs
  runWLSEOpt(size = 5, seedNo = 123, errorFile = tempfile(fileext = ".txt"))
} # }
